initial_prompt: Explain quantum entanglement to me like I'm 5.

messages.content: Explain quantum entanglement to me like I'm 5.

Okay, kiddo, imagine you have two magic coins that are best friends forever. No matter how far apart you take them—one in your pocket and one on the moon—if you flip one and it lands on heads, the other one *instantly* flips to tails. They just "know" what the other is doing, even without talking or sending messages. It's like they're connected by an invisible string that works super fast, faster than anything!

That's quantum entanglement in the tiny world of atoms and particles. Scientists call it "spooky action at a distance" because it's weird and real, but we don't fully understand why it happens yet. If you want to learn more (when you're a bit older), check out fun videos on quantum stuff—it's like science magic! What else are you curious about? 😊
